claim: A freshly installed Linux .deb starts from its installed location, survives a package upgrade without losing user data, and can be purged without leaving package files or deleting that user data.

verification.detail: The hosted job packaged the Linux bundle and ran scripts/test_linux_deb_install.sh for clean apt installs in ubuntu:24.04 and debian:13-slim. It installed a lower-version package, upgraded to the current package, checked the desktop launcher and installed files, launched the app under Xvfb, purged it, and checked package/filesystem cleanup and user-data sentinel preservation.

limitations: Coverage is amd64 Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 slim containers; other distributions and architectures are not established.
The preserved user-data sentinel is a plain text marker, not an .orproj file; this install check does not establish project editing, saving, or recovery semantics.
The launch smoke check establishes startup under Xvfb, not interactive usability, signing, or production release readiness.
